title: WPA-era band and the Kingfish Cabaret on Decatur Street
summary: During WPA days he played with George Lewis and others at the Kingfish Cabaret and rehearsed in the large WPA band.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Where was that? Do you remember about that?
The Kingfish Cabaret. That's on Decatur and, uh, St. Philip.
Oh, is that where the chicken place is now?
That's right. That's right. That's right. And we had Edgar on drum, George Lewis on clarinet, Billy on piano, myself on trumpet. Is that Edgar Mosley?
We was getting a dollar quarter tonight.

No, Billy, Billy, Billy, uh, piano, play the piano. Did he his wife? Billy, yes. Billy, Billy Pierce. Billy, Billy Pierce. That's the name of Billy Pierce. Yeah, that's right. Well, she was playing with us. So, after that, you know, before that, that, uh, I was playing in the WPA band. Now, one of the first men in that band, I, uh, Adolph Alexander, a fella by the name of Garnier, and Tilna, Wilma Tilna. Did you play saxophone? Did you play saxophone then? So, we used to play back there on Claiborne Street in the old garage. That's when they made the band up. Yeah. So, the band come in and get larger and larger and larger until they got a whole group of musicians into, I guess, about a hundred and some other men. That's the time I started playing on here at night in the Kingfish Cabaret, with the Four-Piece Band. We used to rehearse in the WPA band every day on Decatur and, uh, Dumaine. Dumaine and Decatur at, uh, Patonis Place. And, uh, used to play on that night.
